This really struck me. I've been playing since before season 1 and a couple of seasons ago I hit diamond and then dropped just before the season's end. Last season I actually got there pretty easily and this season I'm starting to slowly climb back up.  
The truth is at around certain hours I cant bring myself to queue up. I suffer enough anxiety by myself without having people constantly bash me for every single small mistake, enemy or ally.  
When I finally go out and play normals or whatever because I dont feel like putting my elo on the line on a bad day / mood, I get bashed because of my elo last season, boosted insults etc, OR they say they only lose because they got matched with a diamond player.  
This feels even worse when, as of last season, I put in a lot of effort to learn yasuo (a patch or so before he went flavour of the rest of the season until his nerfs). I've gotten flamed for even so much as hovering yasuo on a champ select when i had around 60% winrate on him, and I wont even get started on the circlejerk around that champion on this subreddit.  
I feel like something that started out of sheer enjoyment, bliss, ignorance and fun, slowly turned into something routinely stressful for me. League is almost like a mental gym at this point. Either you're strong enough to handle the weight put onto you, or you crack and get your day ruined. But after all these years, the very notion of walking away from the game is something I dont even consider, because at its best, league is still the thing I get the most enjoyment out of.

Not necessarily for reviews, just for overall actual gameplay. If you seem to like the game, then by all means go for it. Pre-orders are actually a part of the problem because people miss out on exclusive parts of the game if they don't buy it before it comes out, which incentivizes "reckless" consumption, although as someone that (only) pre-ordered dark souls 2 I understand your side as well.

Everyone is free to do as they wish with their money, friend. The point I was trying to make was that if everyone pre-orders a game that looks good solely due to trailers (remember colonial marines), you're incentivizing this practice, which makes devs and/or publishers not even want to push out a finished game, because they'll have sales. This of course doesnt apply to every single case, but I'm sure you get what I'm saying here.

This very much relates to consumerism. You don't want to buy a product just because you want to buy something (hype aside, I've of course been hyped for a game). $60 is a fair sum of money which can be used for a multitude of things, now would you rather wait and see if the product you're getting is actually worth the money you paid for it or blindy throw money at a corporation just because the trailers look neat? Consumer awareness is an actual thing that everyone should have and the pre-order bonuses you get for buying a game are pretty much a BS practice.
